business_problem: A complex legacy reporting platform limited maternity analytics to three months of data, took more than an hour per query, and required months to add new cross-source reports, delaying care and compliance reporting.
solution_summary: Sydney Local Health District deployed Snowflake AI Data Cloud as a new analytics foundation for its Women and Babies Service so clinicians could query maternity, mortality, morbidity, and intervention data across multiple health systems without waiting on the legacy environment. Datasets derived from electronic medical records and other local sources are centralized in Snowflake, where teams can validate output accuracy, query several years of history, and generate reports for clinicians and Ministry of Health reporting. The platform replaces an environment that only handled the previous three months of data and took months to build new queries, enabling near-real-time analysis instead. Because the same governed store supports both operational decision-making and clinical research, doctors and nurses can respond to delivery trauma or morbidity patterns faster while analysts adapt quickly to new compliance requests.

data_flow: Datasets derived from electronic medical records and other maternity systems are centralized in Snowflake AI Data Cloud, where clinicians and analysts run validated reports across several years of history. business_outcome: SLHD reduced PIBO data query times from over an hour to 55 seconds, expanded analysis from three months to several years of data, provisioned new reports in hours instead of months, and improved the timeliness of maternal and neonatal care decisions.
